newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa prices down as harvest wanes.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa prices down as harvest wanes.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were lower on Wednesday from a week ago on thin buying interest as the mid-crop harvest began to wind down, traders said.
They said cocoa was quoted at 2,650-2,690 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,740-2,770 rupiah a week ago.
"The market is very quiet as the season is coming to an end," one trader said. "The mid-crop harvest is almost over and cocoa arrivals are sharply down."
The trader said there was some short-covering but players were generally in the process of closing their books.
Another trader said that steady rainfall was making it difficult for players to dry their cocoa beans.
Traders said a recent decision by the South Sulawesi governor to stop the trade in unfermented cocoa beans had largely gone unnoticed.
One trader said the governor had last week said that implementation of his decision would be delayed for two years, but this could not be confirmed.
Traders had said that arrivals in South Sulawesi were an estimated 16,800 tonnes in August, 17,330 tonnes in September and 22,000 tonnes in October. November data was not available.
